item.title: High water, high rents: Poorest residents pay the most for climate adaptation
item.description: As cities worldwide adapt to extreme weather, climate adaptation must prevent people from wading through flooded streets in the future. But the costs are not equally shared. A study from the University of Copenhagen shows that climate adaptation policies may even make social inequality worse. In Copenhagen, stormwater costs fall disproportionately on not-for-profit housing residents, as these neighborhoods are often located near climate adaptation projects. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: After years of speculation, Suriname evicts Mennonites farming in the Amazon
item.description: More than 50 Mennonites have been deported from Suriname following years of controversy over plans to establish agricultural settlements for large-scale farming in the Amazon Rainforest. Authorities removed the Mennonites, members of a conservative Christian group that rejects modern technology, from state land in Suriname’s Sipaliwini district. They had been staying in the area with […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: A Florida chimpanzee sanctuary cut off by flooding; uses drone to deliver food to a stranded chimp
item.description: A chimpanzee named Kaleb faced isolation during heavy flooding at Save the Chimps sanctuary. Staff utilized a drone to deliver essential food and blankets to him safely. The floodwaters disrupted normal delivery routes, which required creative solutions to ensure animal welfare. By using trucks and a drone, caregivers managed to keep the animals fed and healthy, despite the challenges. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: ‘Her hands are as cold as ice’: Gaza families struggle to keep warm
item.description: Flooded tents and high prices leave Gaza families struggling to keep children warm as winter approaches. Fuente: Al Jazeera English.

item.title: Smallholder farmers struggle on El Niño frontline; will the world help?
item.description: Smallholder farmers across the globe are bracing for, or already feeling, the effects of a historically strong El Niño. This event — forecast to peak in December with lasting impacts deep into 2027 — has brought warnings of shocks to global food prices and food security. The record-breaking 2026-2027 El Niño could drive an additional […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: "Cómo Israel fabrica la 'crisis' invernal de Gaza": 'Middle East Eye'
item.description: Una vez más, la ya destruida Franja de Gaza hace frente a terribles inundaciones provocadas por las lluvias torrenciales. Con el 65 % de los gazatíes viviendo en tiendas de campaña —cerca de 1,4 millones de personas—, los refugios se han visto inundados o completamente destruidos. Al respecto, 'Middle East Eye' sostiene que Israel ha "fabricado" la crisis invernal al restringir el ingreso de materiales de construcción para prevenir este tipo de escenarios. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.description: Canadian extractive industries have been linked to the displacement of at least 300,000 people in Africa over the past 30 years, the Justice and Corporate Accountability Project (JCAP) said in an October report. item.title: Israel kills six in Gaza hospital strike as 9-month-old baby freezes to death
item.description: An overnight Israeli air strike on Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza killed at least six Palestinians Thursday, including a teenage boy and a surgeon, medics said. Elsewhere in the devastated Palestinian territory, a nine-month-old baby died from the cold as families flee worsening flooding. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Sensors track stress in plants in real time—without hurting them in the process
item.description: Even plants, from towering palm trees to vegetables such as onions and eggplants, can get stressed. Now, a team of engineers has designed a new kind of sensor that attaches directly to plants and peers inside them to track how they respond to stressors such as drought and fires in real time. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Flanked by Greta Thunberg, Rikki Dank says the Australian PM must heed the calls for action on climate change An indigenous climate activist who is taking the Australian government to the UN human rights committee over its coal and gas exports stood alongside Greta Thunberg at Cop summit to demand Anthony Albanese “stop speaking and start listening.” Draped in traditional dress in front of a media throng, Rikki Dank, a Gudanji and Wakaya traditional owner, delivered an impassioned plea to Albanese to listen to “the Australian people when they say no more new coal, oil and gas”. item.description: Industries across the globe are seeking to reduce their carbon footprint and become more sustainable. To do so, many are turning to employees with specific credentials. item.title: First guidelines on attempts to manipulate the ocean put spotlight on geoengineering industry
item.description: Proponents argue ocean carbon removal is necessary to counteract the effects of the climate crisis but critics say more research is needed A cluster of candy cane-striped smoke stacks dots the horizon of Tufts Cove in Nova Scotia, Canada. item.description: Flooding at a chimpanzee sanctuary in Fort Pierce, Florida, has made it difficult for staff to reach some of the animals. Workers have turned to drones to deliver food, including bananas, while large parts of the property remain underwater. Fuente: Euronews.

item.description: A Frontier Airlines flight faced a critical situation as a bathroom sink started leaking profusely mid-air. While en route to Detroit, the crew had to make an emergency landing at Chicago O'Hare International Airport. Footage revealed alarming amounts of water accumulating on the cabin floor, though the aircraft was safely landed without further incident. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: From Romania to Kazakhstan, summer droughts linked to less winter ice in two rapidly warming seas
item.description: This summer, with its scarce rainfall and repeated heat waves, witnessed one of the most severe droughts in Europe since 1540. The resulting wildfires across western Europe received considerable media attention, but eastern Europe was also heavily hit, worsening the humanitarian crisis caused by the war in Ukraine. Simulations have shown that such droughts are bound to become more frequent and severe in the future due to man-made global warming. Fuente: Phys.org.

The nearly 1,000ft American-made vessel, once the fastest ocean liner in the world, was launched in 1952 and made history by setting a transatlantic speed record during its maiden voyage. Under current policies, the planet will heat up by 2.7C on average by the end of the century compared with preindustrial times, the report by Climate Action Tracker (CAT) found. item.description: The latest global State of Wildfires report, co-led by the University of East Anglia, shows that the extreme fire-prone weather experienced across Spain and Portugal in 2025 was three times more likely due to human-caused climate change, and the area burned was three times larger. The paper is published in Earth System Science Data. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Study Links Climate And Violence: Peru skeletons show low conflict; ritual sacrifice stays distinct
item.description: Throughout history, ancient communities in Peru's Lambayeque Valley confronted significant flooding and food scarcity. Interestingly, despite these hardships, instances of interpersonal violence were notably infrequent. Research indicates that only a tiny percentage of skeletal remains revealed signs of conflict. Instead, these resilient societies cleverly adapted, capitalizing on marine resources to weather environmental challenges. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: "Por la economía, para reducir el coste de vida", el slogan a favor de la acción climática en la COP31
item.description: El mensaje, que se repite en la conferencia anual de la ONU, refleja el esfuerzo por captar la atención de Estados y Gobiernos que enfrentan conflictos y crisis que han puesto al cambio climático en un segundo plano en las prioridades. Según el secretario general, se debe alcanzar consenso en torno a cuatro principios: el fin de la dependencia de los combustibles fósiles, la adaptación a un mundo más cálido, elevar el apoyo a los países vulnerables y promover la cooperación frente al conflicto.
